topics.title: High-Level Design of Notification System
topics.description: Understanding the architecture of scalable notification systems using message queues, workers, and external providers.

subtopics.title: Definition
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Definition

🔹 Notification System (Definition)

A distributed, event-driven system that delivers messages to users via push, SMS, or email in a scalable and reliable manner.

subtopics.title: Notification Service (API Layer)
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ Core Components



1. Notification Service (API Layer)

🔹 Definition

A stateless backend service that receives notification requests and routes them to appropriate channels.

🔹 Important Points

Entry point of the system

Validates requests

Checks user preferences

Decides delivery channel

Scales horizontally

🔹 New Terms

Stateless Service
A service that does not store session data locally.
Any request can be handled by any server.

Horizontal Scaling
Adding more servers to handle more traffic.

subtopics.title: Message Queue
subtopics.theory:
2. Message Queue

🔹 Definition

A middleware system that stores messages temporarily and allows asynchronous processing.

🔹 Important Points

Buffers traffic spikes

Decouples producers and consumers

Prevents system overload

Improves reliability

🔹 New Terms

Producer
Component that sends messages to queue.

Consumer (Worker)
Component that reads messages from queue.

Asynchronous Processing
Task is executed later, not immediately.

Decoupling
Separating components so they don’t depend tightly on each other.

subtopics.title: Workers (Consumers)
subtopics.theory:
3. Workers (Consumers)

🔹 Definition

Background processes that fetch messages from queue and send notifications.

🔹 Important Points

Handle retry logic

Format messages

Communicate with third-party services

Can be auto-scaled

subtopics.title: Third-Party Notification Providers
subtopics.theory:
4. Third-Party Notification Providers

🔹 Definition

External services responsible for final delivery.

Examples:

APNs (iOS)

FCM (Android)

SMS gateways

Email providers

🔹 Important Points

We do NOT directly send to devices

Providers may fail

Need retry mechanism

subtopics.title: Database
subtopics.theory:
5. Database

🔹 Definition

Persistent storage used to store user preferences and notification logs.

🔹 Important Points

Stores opt-in/opt-out settings

Stores delivery status

Used for analytics and debugging

subtopics.title: High-Level Flow
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ High-Level Flow (Step-by-Step)



🔁 Notification Delivery Flow

Event occurs (e.g., order placed)

Request sent to Notification Service

Service checks:

User preference

Notification type

Message added to appropriate queue

Worker consumes message

Worker sends message to provider

Provider delivers to user

subtopics.title: Important Design Principles
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Important Design Principles



🔹 Scalability

System should handle millions of notifications/day.

How?

Stateless APIs

Multiple workers

Partitioned queues



🔹 Reliability

No notification should be lost.

How?

Durable queues

Retry mechanism

Dead-letter queues



🔹 Availability

System should remain operational even if some components fail.



🔹 Fault Tolerance

System continues functioning even when part of it crashes.

subtopics.title: Advantages of This Architecture
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Advantages of This Architecture

Advantage

Explanation

High Scalability

Easy to add servers

Reliable

Queue prevents data loss

Flexible

Supports multiple channels

Decoupled

Failures isolated

Handles Traffic Spikes

Queue absorbs load

subtopics.title: Disadvantages
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ Disadvantages

Disadvantage

Explanation

Increased Complexity

More components to manage

Message Ordering Issues

Async processing may reorder

Dependency on Third-Party Services

External failures affect system

Monitoring Overhead

Needs tracking & logging

subtopics.title: Common Interview Discussion Points
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ Common Interview Discussion Points

What if provider fails?

How to prevent duplicate notifications?

How to ensure ordering?

How to handle millions of messages?

What if queue fills up?

subtopics.title: Final Insight
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ One-Line Chapter Insight

A scalable notification system uses a stateless API layer, message queues, asynchronous workers, and external providers to ensure reliable and high-volume message delivery.
